# SPBM, IS-IS and Fabric OAM

_Extreme Fabric Engine · 40 commands_

The Fabric Connect core. IS-IS adjacencies, nicknames, B-VLANs, unicast and multicast FIBs, CFM, l2 ping and l2 traceroute.

## Details

### `show isis adjacencies [verbose]`

```
show isis adjacencies
show isis adjacencies | exclude UP
```

A neighbor stuck in INIT, or missing, usually means one of these: a different manual area, B-VLANs or primary B-VLAN that differ between the switches, a hello-auth mismatch, an MTU problem, the NNI VLAN membership, or a duplicate system-id or nickname. Multi-area boundary nodes accept `home|remote`.


### `show isis spbm`

On a vIST pair, check that the peer system-id and virtual B-MAC match on both peers.


### `show isis spbm nick-name [home | remote]`

```
show isis spbm nick-name
show isis spbm nick-name | include SW-ACCESS
```

Look up a nickname from another output (for example a remote MAC entry) and get the switch name. The output also lists the virtual B-MACs, so it shows the vIST pairs.


### `show isis spbm unicast-fib [b-mac <bmac>] [vlan <bvid>] [summary]`

Each node should appear in both B-VLANs. Different outgoing interfaces per B-VLAN are normal (ECT load sharing).


### `show isis lsdb [sysid <xxxx.xxxx.xxxx>] [detail] [tlv <n>]`

```
show isis lsdb
show isis lsdb sysid 0200.0000.0101 detail
```

A sequence number that keeps increasing fast on one node means that node is flapping. With `tlv 185` or `tlv 186` you can inspect the advertised IP routes. Since 9.4, `detail` also shows the L2 VSN mapping bit for TLVs 185/186.


### `show debug spbm isis spf-log`

Many SPF runs in a short time point to a flapping link or node. Compare the times with `show logging file`.


### `show isis int-counters`

Increasing authentication failures point to a hello-auth key or type mismatch. Reset the counters with `clear isis stats`.


### `show isis manual-area`

Multi-area boundary nodes use `show isis area` (home and remote area).


### `isis dup-detection-temp-disable`

A duplicate nickname or system-id makes the switch drop IS-IS. Fix the duplicate value; this command only gives you time to do it. Check the remaining time with `show isis dup-detection-temp-disable remaining-time`.


### `router isis`

```
vlan create 4051 name "BVLAN-1" type spbm-bvlan
vlan create 4052 name "BVLAN-2" type spbm-bvlan
spbm
router isis
  spbm 1
  spbm 1 nick-name 1.01.01
  spbm 1 b-vid 4051-4052 primary 4051
  system-id 0200.0001.0101
  manual-area 49.0001
  sys-name SW-CORE-01
  exit
router isis enable
```

The official order for bringing up a fabric node by hand: create the B-VLANs, enable spbm, set up the SPBM instance, area and system-id, then router isis enable. Always use two B-VLANs. The nickname, system-id and IS-IS hostname must be unique in the fabric. Change the default system-id (the B-MAC) to something you can recognize. Most sites assign nicknames through Zero Touch Fabric or a nickname server instead.


### `spbm 1 nick-name <x.xx.xx>`

> ▲ **Caution:** Changing it on a live switch briefly disrupts the fabric services of that node.


### `spbm 1 b-vid <bvid1>-<bvid2> primary <bvid1>`

The B-VLAN IDs and the primary B-VLAN must be the same on every node, otherwise no adjacency forms. Create the B-VLANs with `vlan create <id> type spbm-bvlan`.


### `system-id <xxxx.xxxx.xxxx>`

> ▲ **Caution:** Needs `no router isis enable` first, so the switch drops out of the fabric.


### `isis spbm 1 l1-metric <1-16777215 | auto>`

```
interface gigabitEthernet 1/49
isis spbm 1 l1-metric 5000
```

The default `auto` derives the cost from the port speed. Raise the metric on a link before maintenance to move traffic away from it gracefully.


### `isis / isis spbm 1 / isis enable`

```
interface gigabitEthernet 1/49
no shutdown
isis
isis spbm 1
isis enable
```

The same three commands work on an MLT (`interface mlt <id>`). A manual NNI is normally not a member of any VLAN.


### `isis hello-auth type hmac-sha-256 key <key>`

Auto-sense ports use the global `auto-sense isis hello-auth type ...` instead. Since 9.2 an Auto-sense port with a key mismatch goes to the NNI-AUTH-FAIL state.


### `overload`

Drain a core or BCB node before maintenance; remove it with `no overload`. Services that end on this switch (BEB) still work.

> ▲ **Caution:** All transit traffic moves to other paths. Check that they have enough capacity.


### `spbm 1 ip enable`

Pair it with `ip-source-address <clip>` and `redistribute direct` in IS-IS Router Config to advertise GRT routes.


### `redistribute direct [route-map <map>] / isis apply redistribute direct`

```
router isis
  redistribute direct
  redistribute direct enable
  exit
isis apply redistribute direct
```

The redistribution only takes effect after `isis apply redistribute <protocol> [vrf <name>]` (User EXEC). This step is easy to forget. Check the result with `show ip isis redistribute`.


### `cfm spbm enable`

```
cfm spbm mepid 101
cfm spbm enable
```

Only switches with CFM enabled answer. A hop without CFM is missing from the trace. Use a unique MEP ID per switch (802.1ag requires unique MEP IDs within an MA).


### `l2 ping vlan <bvid> routernodename <isis-hostname>`

```
l2 ping vlan 4051 routernodename SW-ACCESS-12
l2 ping vlan 4052 routernodename SW-ACCESS-12 burst-count 10
```

Test both B-VLANs, because they can take different paths.


### `l2 traceroute vlan <bvid> routernodename <isis-hostname>`

```
l2 traceroute vlan 4051 routernodename SW-ACCESS-12
```


### `l2 traceroute ip-address <ip> [vrf <vrf>]`

```
l2 traceroute ip-address 10.20.30.40 vrf CORP
```

This only works when the next hop to the IP is an IS-IS route to a remote BEB. If you get "MEP does not exist" in a VRF, the route is probably not learned through IS-IS. On a DvR leaf the output may only show the DvR controllers. (The VRF hint comes from the Extreme community forum; the DvR note is from the official command reference.)


### `l2 tracetree <bvid> <isid> [routernodename <name>]`

```
l2 tracetree 4051 20100
```


### `l2 ping anycast-gw <isid> [vrf <vrf>]`

`l2 traceroute anycast-gw <isid>` does the trace.


### `spbm nick-name server`

Set the range with `spbm nick-name server prefix <x.x0.00>`. Clients without a static nickname get one automatically. Configure at least two servers for redundancy.


### `show isis int-auth`

Compare both ends of a link that does not come up. For Auto-sense NNIs, the global `show auto-sense isis` applies.


### `show spbm nick-name server leases`

Run it on the nickname server switch. A switch without a static nickname that is missing here never got one.
